memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have had daily itchy wheals for the past year, worse in the evenings. I work with flowers and notice flare-ups after handling certain plants. No known food triggers. I take occasional antihistamine but symptoms persist.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked with Dr Suresh Menon (D05) for 2025-04-05 at 10:30 AM. Reason: evaluation of chronic urticaria.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria.
Patient reports daily pruritic wheals, worse evenings, associated with floral work. Examination shows scattered transient wheals across trunk and limbs, no angioedema. Vital signs normal. Smoking status: never. No inhaler use. Plan: start levocetirizine 5 mg OD and cetirizine 10 mg HS; advise non‑sedating antihistamine regimen, avoid known triggers, follow‑up in 8 weeks. Labs: CBC with eosinophils, thyroid function test.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
levocetirizine 5 mg tablet, take one tablet by mouth once daily.
cetirizine 10 mg tablet, take one tablet by mouth at bedtime.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria.
Patient reports reduced wheal frequency, now 3‑4 days per week, less intense itching. Examination shows occasional faint wheals on arms. Smoking status: never. Plan: continue levocetirizine 5 mg OD, increase cetirizine to 10 mg BID for breakthrough symptoms; reinforce trigger avoidance. Review in 2 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
levocetirizine 5 mg tablet, take one tablet by mouth once daily.
cetirizine 10 mg tablet, take one tablet by mouth twice daily.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Hemoglobin 13.9 g/dl, WBC 6.0 x10^9/l, eosinophils 0.3 x10^9/l (0.0‑0.5). Platelets 208 x10^9/l.
TSH 2.0 µIU/ml, Free T4 1.1 ng/dl.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria.
Patient states urticaria now occurs only 1‑2 days per week, mild. No angioedema. Examination clear of active wheals. Smoking status: never. Plan: taper cetirizine to 10 mg HS only; continue levocetirizine 5 mg OD. Advise to monitor and return if symptoms worsen. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
levocetirizine 5 mg tablet, take one tablet by mouth once daily.
cetirizine 10 mg tablet, take one tablet by mouth at bedtime.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment changed: next visit rescheduled from 2025-12-01 to 2025-12-10 at 11:00 AM with Dr Suresh Menon (D05).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria.
Patient reports occasional mild wheals (<1 day per week), well controlled. Examination shows no active lesions. Smoking status: never. Plan: maintain levocetirizine 5 mg OD, cetirizine 10 mg HS PRN for breakthrough. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
levocetirizine 5 mg tablet, take one tablet by mouth once daily.
cetirizine 10 mg tablet, take one tablet by mouth at bedtime as needed.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Hemoglobin 13.7 g/dl, WBC 5.8 x10^9/l, eosinophils 0.2 x10^9/l (0.0‑0.5). Platelets 212 x10^9/l.
TSH 2.2 µIU/ml, Free T4 1.2 ng/dl.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria.
Patient asymptomatic for past 6 weeks, no wheals or itching. Examination clear. Smoking status: never. Plan: attempt cetirizine discontinuation; continue levocetirizine 5 mg OD. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: levocetirizine 5 mg tablet, take one tablet by mouth once daily.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria.
Patient remains symptom‑free off cetirizine, on levocetirizine only. No wheals reported. Examination negative for skin lesions. Smoking status: never. Plan: continue levocetirizine 5 mg OD, consider trial off medication in 2 months if remains clear. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria.
Patient reports no symptoms for 3 months off cetirizine, still on levocetirizine 5 mg OD. Examination clear. Smoking status: never. Plan: levocetirizine 5 mg OD continued, advise to monitor for relapse. Review as needed.
